newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK leadership debate heats up as lawmaker ejected.
newsitem.headline: HK leadership debate heats up as lawmaker ejected.

text.p: A Hong Kong lawmaker was ejected from the legislature on Wednesday after he criticised members of two China-backed bodies during a debate on the selection of the British territory's first post-colonial leader.

Independent legislator Leung Yiu-chung was ordered to leave the Legislative Council (Legco) chamber after saying members of the Preparatory and Selection committees were "like foul grass growing out of a foul can", Hong Kong government radio reported.
Leung acknowledged he was referring to some Legco members but refused to withdraw his statement, it said.
The 400 members of the Selection Committee, most of whom were chosen by the Beijing-appointed Preparatory Committee, will name the chief executive on December 11.
Their choice will replace Governor Chris Patten when Britain hands back the territory to Beijing on July 1, 1997, ending 150 years of colonial rule.
The leading contenders for the top post are shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa, former chief justice Ti Liang Yang, former appeals court judge Simon Li and businessman Peter Woo.

Hong Kong's pro-democracy camp has criticised the selection process as a sham. The appointment of the Selection Committee in Beijing -- with its heavy leaning towards Hong Kong's business community and vocal supporters of China -- prompted demonstrations in the territory.

Hong Kong's largest political party, the Democratic Party, said on Wednesday it plans protests to greet Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen when he visits the territory on Friday for a meeting of the Selection Committee.
